In the late 1960s and 1970s, alongside mathematician Roger Penrose, Hawking applied general relativity to the concept of black holes, proving that space and time would have a beginning in the Big Bang and an end in black holes. 

His most groundbreaking theoretical discovery came in 1974, when he calculated that black holes are not completely black. By combining quantum mechanics with Einstein's theory of gravity, he demonstrated that black holes emit thermal radiation—a phenomenon now known as **"Hawking Radiation."** This revelation reshaped modern astrophysics and launched the ongoing quest for a unified "Theory of Everything."

Hawking became the Lucasian Professor of Mathematics at Cambridge in 1979—a prestigious post once held by Sir Isaac Newton. 

Despite losing his speech following a emergency tracheostomy in 1985, Hawking adapted. Communicating through a trademark computerized voice synthesizer operated by a cheek switch, he published *A Brief History of Time* in 1988. The book spent a record-breaking 237 weeks on the *Sunday Times* bestseller list, selling over 10 million copies and transforming Hawking into a global pop-culture icon and the world's most recognizable scientist.

---

### In His Own Words: Mind Over Matter

Throughout his life, Hawking’s physical limitations stood in stark contrast to his boundless optimism and razor-sharp wit. His outlook on his illness and work has provided some of the most enduring quotes in modern science:

* **On his initial terminal diagnosis:**
  > *"My expectations were reduced to zero when I was 21. Everything since then has been a bonus. Although I was a cloud over my future, I found, to my surprise, that I was enjoying life in the present much more than before."*

* **On living with ALS:**
  > *"My advice to other disabled people would be, concentrate on things your disability doesn't prevent you doing well, and don't regret the things it interferes with. Don't be disabled in spirit, as well as physically."*

* **On the mysteries of existence:**
  > *"The universe doesn't allow perfection... We are just an advanced breed of monkeys on a minor planet of a very average star. But we can understand the Universe. That makes us something very special."*

* **On humor and resilience:**
  > *"Life would be tragic if it weren't funny."*

---

### The World Awaits Word

As messages of support pour in from world leaders, fellow scientists, and admirers across the globe, colleagues at Cambridge remain hopeful. Hawking’s life has been a relentless sequence of beating the odds—not only surviving a disease that should have claimed him in his twenties, but using his time to rewrite the laws of cosmology.

"Stephen is a fighter," said a close colleague at the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics. "He has stared into the void of the universe and into the face of his own mortality for 45 years. If anyone can pull through this, it is Stephen."

For now, the world waits and watches, hopeful that the voice that explained the cosmos will soon speak to us once again.

***

*(Historical Note: Stephen Hawking successfully recovered from this April 2009 health crisis and was discharged from the hospital the following month. He continued his scientific work, writing, and public advocacy for nearly another decade before passing away peacefully on March 14, 2018, at the age of 76.)*
